title: SARIS: Accelerating Stencil Computations on Energy-Efficient RISC-V Compute Clusters with Indirect Stream Registers
problem: Stencil codes suffer from significant address calculation and irregular memory access overheads that limit performance in compute-intensive applications.
motivation: Stencil codes are performance-critical in many compute-intensive applications, making their acceleration essential.
method: SARIS accelerates stencil computations (algorithms that repeatedly apply a pattern to grid elements) on RISC-V compute clusters using register-mapped indirect streams—special CPU registers that encode memory access patterns. These registers capture irregular memory accesses (non-sequential, unpredictable patterns where addresses depend on data values) so the processor doesn't have to recalculate addresses repeatedly. By pre-encoding these patterns into fast CPU registers, the system eliminates the address calculation overhead that normally limits stencil performance.
key_novelty: Register-mapped indirect stream registers—special CPU registers that pre-encode memory patterns—eliminate address calculation overhead in stencil computations on RISC-V architectures.
contributions: SARIS methodology for stencil acceleration leveraging register-mapped indirect stream registers
Achieves 2.72x speedup and near-ideal 81% FPU utilization on 8-core RISC-V cluster with 1.58x energy efficiency improvement
Demonstrates scalability to 256-core system with 2.14x speedup and 64% FPU utilization, outperforming leading GPU code generators
primary_theme: Stencil acceleration via indirect stream registers
